content.title: About
content.content: Potato hash brown is a dish made from grated potatoes that are pan‑fried or deep‑fried until crisp and golden. It is commonly served as a side or snack in restaurants, offering a crunchy exterior and a soft interior, usually seasoned with salt and spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first recorded recipes for shredded potato dishes date back to the 19th century in the United States.
Hash browns are a staple breakfast item in American diners and fast‑food chains.
There are many variations: with cheese, bacon, onions, or herbs.
In some countries they are shaped into round patties, in others they are served as flat cakes.
Hash browns can be cooked in oil or baked in the oven for a lighter version.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide complex carbs that supply lasting energy and help keep you feeling full.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hash browns contain vitamin B6 and folate, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are a good source of potassium, important for blood pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Low sodium (when lightly salted)
items.content: If prepared with minimal added salt, hash browns can fit into a balanced diet.

items.title: Fiber
items.content: Grated potatoes retain some dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie content when fried
items.content: Cooking in oil adds significant calories and fat, so portion size should be monitored.

items.title: Rare potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Over‑cooking at high temperatures can produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound; aim for a golden‑brown color, not dark brown.

items.title: Salt
items.content: Excessive salt can contribute to hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hash browns are served hot as a side to meat, fish or vegetables, used in burgers, or enjoyed as a snack with dips such as ketchup, mayo, or ranch dressing. They can also be crumbled over salads for added crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked hash browns in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. Frozen hash browns keep up to 3 months; they can be cooked directly from frozen without fully thawing.
